en: If you dropped a feather and a hammer in the vacuum of the Moon, they would hit the ground at the exact same time.
The Earth's geographic North Pole is actually a magnetic south pole, which is why the north end of a compass needle points toward it.
Light travels so fast that it takes only about 1.3 seconds for sunlight reflected off the Moon to reach our eyes on Earth.
Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air because the liquid's molecules are packed much more closely together.
A raw lemon can power a small digital clock because its citric acid acts as an electrolyte to conduct electrical current.
A hovercraft uses a fan to trap a cushion of air underneath it, drastically reducing friction so it can glide over land and water.
A sharp knife acts as a wedge, concentrating your downward force into a tiny area to easily slice through a tough apple.
Water has a high specific heat capacity, meaning ocean water absorbs solar heat much slower than the dry sand on a sunny beach.
A stretched archery bow stores elastic potential energy, which instantly transforms into the kinetic energy of the arrow when the string is released.
A single fixed pulley changes the direction of your pulling force, allowing you to pull down with your body weight to raise a flag.
When a metal ball is heated, it undergoes thermal expansion and gets slightly larger, preventing it from passing through a ring it previously fit inside.
Your body converts the chemical energy stored in food into kinetic energy for running and thermal energy to keep you warm.
